# EDA summary (generated by src/eda.py)

Grid 5° × month; QC: footprint SZA > 100°, VZA ≤ 60°. 37,898 observed cell-months over 68 months (22,562 pre-gap, 15,336 post-gap).

## 1. What CLARA measures (sample level)
- **Only night-side samples are credible.** Against ERA5 at the same UTC hour, daylit footprints (SZA < 90°) read +84 W m⁻² (pre-gap) / +69 W m⁻² (post-gap) more than night-side ones (SZA > 100°). The hour-matched ERA5 already contains the real day–night OLR difference, so this excess is instrumental (shortwave contamination). The steepest change lies between ~92° and ~103° (physics_sza.png); 5% of the QC'd samples have SZA in (100°, 105°], where post-gap values still drift slightly (possible residual twilight).
- **Not angle-corrected.** Relative to night-time ERA5, CLARA falls steeply beyond VZA ≈ 60° (physics_vza.png). Within the kept range (VZA ≤ 60°) the binned difference still spans 50 W m⁻² (pre-gap) and 22 W m⁻² (post-gap). VZA is not an allowed predictor, so this residual geometry effect becomes noise.
- **The regime step is calibration, not geometry.** At the same viewing angles (VZA 40–55°), CLARA − ERA5 night is -72 W m⁻² pre-gap but -30 W m⁻² post-gap.
- **The observing geometry drifts.** Satellite altitude, local solar time of the night samples, VZA distribution and daylit fraction all change (physics_geometry.png).

## 2. Agreement with ERA5 (cell-months, area-weighted)
- **Pooled, CLARA vs ERA5 night:** r = 0.333, bias -62.9 W m⁻², RMSE 77.4 W m⁻², slope 0.42.
- **By period:** pre-gap bias -77.1 W m⁻², r 0.44; post-gap bias -35.6 W m⁻², r 0.41. The step sits inside the 2021-09 → 2022-05 gap (temporal_global.png). Within each period CLARA does follow the ERA5 sampling-matched monthly fluctuations.
- **Night-time vs 24 h ERA5:** night-time ERA5 is only marginally closer to CLARA. r 0.333 vs 0.331; RMSE 77.4 vs 79.0 W m⁻². It is still the physically matched predictor, but the choice is not what limits agreement.
- **Reference check, ERA5 24 h vs CERES on the same cell-months:** bias +2.4 W m⁻², r 0.993, RMSE 4.7 W m⁻². ERA5 and the independent observations agree, so the CLARA–ERA5 discrepancies belong to CLARA (calibration, geometry, sampling).
- **Spatial structure is heavily damped in CLARA.** Its zonal-mean profile has the right shape (r = 0.93 with ERA5 night) but only 56% of ERA5's equator-to-pole range (spatial_zonal.png). Its mean map shows little of ERA5's regional structure (spatial_means.png).

## 3. Effective resolution and smoothing
- **Along track:** CLARA samples correlate at r = 0.88 at 232 km, and the CLARA − ERA5 residual reaches 1/e at ~1,933 km. Neighbouring samples share most of their signal: a wide footprint plus synoptic weather.
- **Smoothing ERA5 with spherical caps** raises the agreement with CLARA modestly. Pooled r peaks at R = 600 km (0.337 vs 0.333 unsmoothed); the within-band anomaly r peaks at R = 1000 km (0.291 vs 0.273). The optimum is interior to the candidate set, so the candidates bracket it. An effective footprint scale of ~10³ km is plausible for a wide-field radiometer at ~550–600 km. The radius is chosen per CV fold on training rows only.
- **Grid size** (resolution_grid.csv): 1°: r 0.30, 188,490 cell-months, median 1 overpasses; 2°: r 0.32, 136,814 cell-months, median 1 overpasses; 5°: r 0.33, 37,898 cell-months, median 2 overpasses; 10°: r 0.36, 14,131 cell-months, median 3 overpasses. Coarser cells average more overpasses (less noise) but leave fewer, larger cells. 5° keeps several overpasses per cell-month and is no finer than CLARA's effective resolution. No grid interpolates or upsamples either dataset.
- **Neighbouring-cell correlation** in the same month (resolution_neighbours.csv): CLARA east 0.48; ERA5 night east 0.99; CLARA north 0.61; ERA5 night north 0.92. Monthly ERA5 fields are very smooth; CLARA cell-months are dominated by sampling noise.

## 4. Dependence scales → CV design
- **Spatial residual correlogram** (CLARA minus a linear ERA5 fit, month means removed): fitted 0.35·exp(−d / 1,056 km). The structured part has a range of ~1,056 km, and the nugget (sampling noise) takes ~65% of the residual variance (spatial_correlogram.png). Pre-gap range 1,201 km, post-gap 943 km.
- **Temporal residual autocorrelation** at a fixed cell (same residual as the spatial correlogram; the persistent spatial pattern is included): lag 1 month r = 0.15, lag 2 months r = 0.09, lag 6 months r = 0.01, lag 12 months r = 0.11. Relative to the noise-free part (≈ 0.35 at zero distance), this measures how long the structured discrepancy at a location persists.
- **Day to day** (daily cell means of CLARA − hour-matched ERA5, period means removed): lag-1 day r = 0.30; the within-cell-month SD of daily means is 34 W m⁻². This is weather and noise that monthly ERA5 cannot explain; the noise term absorbs it.
- **Chosen CV settings:**
  - Spatial blocks 60° × 60° (~6,672 km on a side, ≈ 6.3× the fitted range). Spatial buffer 1500 km (fitted range rounded up: 1,500 km).
  - Temporal windows 6 months with ±1 month buffer. The windows hold out whole half-years, so the seasonal and regime structure must be generalised from other years, not interpolated from adjacent months; the buffer removes the adjacent months where the fixed-cell residual correlation is highest.
  - Joint blocks 60° × 60° × 6 months with 1500 km / ±1 month halo.

## 5. Implications for combining the datasets
1. Pair CLARA with ERA5 night-time OLR of the same cell and month. The gain over the 24 h mean is small but the pairing is physically correct.
2. Keep only night-side, VZA ≤ 60° samples. Aggregate to cell-month means and carry the number of overpasses into the noise model, because samples on one overpass are not independent.
3. Expect a large, period-dependent offset and a slope well below 1 (CLARA's spatial contrasts are damped). ERA5 enters through a linear mean function. The step across the gap enters the mean function as a post-gap indicator (β₂, gp.gap_step; the gap months count as post-gap); the long-term time component of the GP absorbs the remaining drift.
4. The structured CLARA–ERA5 discrepancy has a ~10³ km range and little month-to-month memory. Sampling noise dominates single cell-months, so gains from the GP's covariance over the mean function are expected mainly near observed data. Blocked CV with buffers is essential to measure this honestly.
5. Residual geometry effects and day-to-day weather remain as noise. Predictive calibration must be checked, not assumed.
